article_title: MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing
citation: Yuhao Jia, Duantengchuan Li, Jinsong Chen, Zhongjie Mao, Mingwen Tong, Yue Li, Xiaoguang Wang. (2026). MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08697
title: MBP-KT: a meta-behavioral pattern-aware framework for extracting and injecting global collaborative information in knowledge tracing
description: MBP-KT is a three-component framework for knowledge tracing. It first applies a meta-behavioral operator transformation that maps adjacent interactions into Start, Same and Diff operators, decoupling knowledge states from specific questions. It then extracts frequently occurring behavior patterns via a sliding window into a global collaborative pattern matrix, and finally injects the resulting prior into RNN, memory-network, Transformer and state-based KT models. The article states it 'provides general injection strategies to introduce the extracted global collaborative information into various downstream KT models, ensuring the universality of the collaborative information.'
requirements: Requires raw interaction sequences with question, knowledge-concept set and binary correctness, and a training set from which frequent meta-behavioral patterns can be mined with a sliding window and minimum frequency threshold
constraints: The framework targets sequential-model-based KT approaches; injection is described for RNN, memory network, Transformer and state-based families
Gains depend on dataset characteristics: the article attributes smaller gains on XES3G5M to its larger number of knowledge concepts influencing meta-behavioral sequence construction
target_learners: learners whose interaction logs are modeled in knowledge tracing systems
target_learning_goals: predicting learners' knowledge states and next-question performance
examples: On ASSISTments2009, EdNet-KT1 and XES3G5M, MBP-KT-enhanced versions of DKT, DKVMN, AKT, SAINT, UKT, ReKT and Mamba were compared against the base models under an identical training configuration
key_sources: Yuhao Jia, Duantengchuan Li, Jinsong Chen, Zhongjie Mao, Mingwen Tong, Yue Li, Xiaoguang Wang. (2026). MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08697

article_title: MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing
citation: Yuhao Jia, Duantengchuan Li, Jinsong Chen, Zhongjie Mao, Mingwen Tong, Yue Li, Xiaoguang Wang. (2026). MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08697
title: Three real-world KT benchmark datasets: ASSISTments2009, EdNet-KT1 and XES3G5M
description: The article evaluates MBP-KT on three widely-used educational datasets spanning different scales and sparsity levels: ASSISTments2009 (5,766 learners, 13,441 questions, 412,332 interactions, 99.47% sparsity), EdNet-KT1 (6,609 learners, 12,100 questions, 2,148,355 interactions, 97.31% sparsity), and XES3G5M (18,066 learners, 7,645 questions, 5,168,974 interactions, 96.26% sparsity). Evaluation used a single-point prediction protocol with maximum sequence length L=30, and sequences shorter than 5 interactions were filtered out.
requirements: Interaction sequences partitioned into non-overlapping segments of maximum length 30; sequences with fewer than 5 interactions filtered out prior to training
constraints: The learner-question interaction matrix sparsity remains exceptionally high across all datasets, ranging from 96.26% and peaking at 99.47% on ASSISTments2009
target_learners: learners on online tutoring and exercise platforms represented in the three datasets
target_learning_goals: predicting next-question response correctness from historical interaction logs
examples: Training used an identical fixed configuration for all models: Adam optimizer without weight decay, learning rate 1×10−3, batch size 32, 5 epochs
key_sources: Yuhao Jia, Duantengchuan Li, Jinsong Chen, Zhongjie Mao, Mingwen Tong, Yue Li, Xiaoguang Wang. (2026). MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing. Preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08697

article_title: Fostering engineering and science students’ and teachers’ systems thinking and conceptual modeling skills
citation: Peretz, R., Tal, M., Akiri, E., Dori, D., & Dori, Y. J. (2023). Fostering engineering and science students' and teachers' systems thinking and conceptual modeling skills. Instructional Science, 51, 509–543. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-023-09625-9
title: Theoretical and practical frameworks for integrating cross-disciplinary model-based systems engineering online assignments into engineering and science curricula
description: The article's stated contribution is "the formation of theoretical and practical frameworks for the integration of an cross-disciplinary model-based systems engineering online assignments into engineering and science curricula". The framework rests on the premise that next generation science standards include systems thinking and systems modeling among 21st century skills, and operationalizes integration through short online assignment sequences using OPM conceptual modeling. It positions model-based systems learning as achievable across engineering and science settings, including for learners without prior relevant background.
requirements: Integration requires online assignments that are cross-disciplinary and grounded in a model-based systems engineering approach such as OPM.
constraints: The framework was developed and tested with engineering students and engineering and science teachers (55 participants) in food-related assignments; other curricular contexts are not tested in the supplied text.
target_learning_goals: systems thinking
systems modeling
conceptual modeling skills
examples: The study instantiated the framework with four food-related online assignments and OPM models, analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively.
key_sources: Peretz, R., Tal, M., Akiri, E., Dori, D., & Dori, Y. J. (2023). Fostering engineering and science students' and teachers' systems thinking and conceptual modeling skills. Instructional Science, 51, 509–543. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-023-09625-9

article_title: What can moment-by-moment learning curves tell about students’ self-regulated learning?
citation: Inge Molenaar, Anne Horvers, Ryan S. Baker. (2021). What can moment-by-moment learning curves tell about students' self-regulated learning? Learning and Instruction, 72, 101206. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2019.05.003
title: Moment-by-moment learning curves as personalized visualizations of students' accuracy regulation in hybrid human-system self-regulated learning with ALTs.
description: Moment-by-moment learning curves visualize "the probability that a student learned a specific skill at a particular problem during learning", derived automatically from ALT log data via Bayesian Knowledge Tracing and the P(J) estimate. Distinct from classic learning curves, they show "a distillation of student progress" rather than accuracy or effort directly. The article frames them as personalized visualizations that could help learners make valid inferences about how their effort and accuracy relate to progress, addressing utilization deficiency in a hybrid form of human-system regulation where the ALT executes part of the control and monitoring loop.
requirements: Log data from an adaptive learning technology capturing per-problem correctness and knowledge estimates, sufficient practice opportunities per subskill (graphs with 15 or more problems were included).
constraints: The studied ALT's only adaptive mechanism was problem selection; it offered no scaffolding, prompting or error classification.
The curves did not show effort directly, and no associations between curve form and effort were found in this study.
target_learners: Primary education students (grade five, ages 10-12) practicing arithmetic with adaptive learning technologies
target_learning_goals: Self-regulated learning of arithmetic subskills, including regulation of effort and accuracy during practice
examples: In the study, 265 curves coded into four forms were differentially associated with accuracy, prior knowledge, gain and transfer, supporting the curves' value as indicators of accuracy regulation.
key_sources: Inge Molenaar, Anne Horvers, Ryan S. Baker. (2021). What can moment-by-moment learning curves tell about students' self-regulated learning? Learning and Instruction, 72, 101206. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2019.05.003

article_title: A Novel Framework for the Generation of Multiple Choice Question Stems Using Semantic and Machine-Learning Techniques
citation: Praveen Kumar, A., Nayak, A., Shenoy K., M., Chaitanya, & Ghosh, K. (2024). A Novel Framework for the Generation of Multiple Choice Question Stems Using Semantic and Machine-Learning Techniques. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-023-00333-6
title: MBT three-stage Cloze generation pipeline (sentence selection, key-sentence classification, Naive Bayes keyword selection)
description: MBT converts preprocessed textbook sentences into Cloze stems in three stages. A subject expert's Topic_list filters sentences; then five classifiers pick key sentences — the article notes that "the five classifiers- SVM, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), and Logistic Regression (LR) are trained, and the classification is done", using features Sentence Length, Nouns, Abbreviations, and Appendix Words, with a 75%-25% train-test split over cross-validation. Finally a Naive Bayes classifier ranks candidate words by blank-substitution probability, and the top three words per key sentence become Cloze blanks.
requirements: A manually created Topic_list from a subject expert; training data with the Feature_set (SL 100–200 characters, NN, ABR, AW)
constraints: Only the first three ranked words per key sentence become blanks, so n key sentences yield three Cloze stems each
target_learners: students assessed with Cloze MCQs in technical courses
target_learning_goals: automated generation of grammatically correct Cloze assessment items
examples: In the sample run, sentence S1 was selected (SL criteria met, AW present) and produced three Cloze stems blanking 'binding', 'swapped', and 'addresses'
key_sources: Praveen Kumar, A., Nayak, A., Shenoy K., M., Chaitanya, & Ghosh, K. (2024). A Novel Framework for the Generation of Multiple Choice Question Stems Using Semantic and Machine-Learning Techniques. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-023-00333-6

article_title: The effect of programming on primary school students’ mathematical and scientific understanding: educational use of mBot
citation: Sáez-López, J.-M., Sevillano-García, M.-L., & Vazquez-Cano, E. (2019). The effect of programming on primary school students’ mathematical and scientific understanding: educational use of mBot. Education Tech Research Dev, 67, 1405–1425. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09648-5
title: mBot robot with mBlock visual programming environment
description: The mBot is an inexpensive educational robot built on an Arduino UNO board, programmed through mBlock, "a variant adapted to Scratch 2.0" that adds a 'robots' block category. It includes brightness, proximity and line-following sensors, two RGB LEDs, a buzzer and a button. The study used it in sixth-grade math and science units for engine-control and ultrasonic-sensor activities with immediate feedback.
requirements: Visual block programming environment (mBlock, adapted from Scratch 2.0) so primary students can program intuitively
constraints: Authors position it as suitable from levels 3–4 of primary education onwards; science-area integration showed no significant learning gains
target_learning_goals: computational concepts such as sequences, loops and conditionals
integer and coordinate understanding in mathematics
examples: Keyboard arrow-key engine-control activity with speeds 50, 100 and 255
Ultrasonic-sensor obstacle-avoidance activity using a conditional and a loop
key_sources: Sáez-López, J.-M., Sevillano-García, M.-L., & Vazquez-Cano, E. (2019). The effect of programming on primary school students’ mathematical and scientific understanding: educational use of mBot. Education Tech Research Dev, 67, 1405–1425. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-019-09648-5

article_title: A framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment in vocational education
citation: Sebastiaan de Klerk, Bernard P. Veldkamp, Theo J. H. M. Eggen. (2018). A framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment in vocational education. Education Tech Research Dev (2018) 66:147–171. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-017-9559-5
title: A two-stage framework for MBPA design and development in vocational education
description: The article introduces a comprehensive framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment, uniting assessment development and multimedia development theory with a sole focus on vocational education. As printed: "The framework therefore comprises two general stages: analysis and design and development and administration , both involving different processes." The first stage, guided by assessment and subject matter experts, proceeds through seven steps from determining purposes and constructs to constructing the measurement model; the second stage, guided by multimedia experts, covers ICT development, task building, implementation, pretesting, and fitness-for-purpose evaluation. Unlike ECD, it offers a step-by-step approach while remaining iterative.
requirements: A multidisciplinary team including assessment experts, subject matter experts, psychometricians, and multimedia experts working across both stages
constraints: The framework was developed for and focuses solely on vocational education, though the authors state it can be used in other settings
target_learning_goals: procedural and manual skills currently measured by performance-based assessment
examples: The framework was used to rebuild a pilot MBPA for confined space guards in Dutch vocational education
key_sources: Sebastiaan de Klerk, Bernard P. Veldkamp, Theo J. H. M. Eggen. (2018). A framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment in vocational education. Education Tech Research Dev (2018) 66:147–171. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-017-9559-5

article_title: A framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment in vocational education
citation: Sebastiaan de Klerk, Bernard P. Veldkamp, Theo J. H. M. Eggen. (2018). A framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment in vocational education. Education Tech Research Dev (2018) 66:147–171. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-017-9559-5
title: Multimedia-based performance assessment (MBPA)
description: MBPA is an innovative assessment type that blends computer-based testing and performance-based assessment. Using multimedia such as animation, video, and virtual reality, students are immersed in a virtual environment in which they complete tasks or achieve objectives while navigating that environment. The article states: "MBPA includes a whole range of new response types for logging actual student behavior in the tasks—for example, speed, clicking behavior, navigational behavior through the virtual environment, typing, eye-tracking, and accuracy." MBPA is used to measure vocational skills currently measured by performance-based assessment, offering an alternative with more interaction between student and computer than other CBT.
requirements: An ICT infrastructure able to incorporate and present multimedia and innovative items, including a virtual interface that can incorporate movies, animations, and avatars
constraints: The article emphasizes this need not refer to immersive virtual environments as in serious games or simulations
target_learners: vocational education students, such as confined space guards in training
target_learning_goals: procedural and manual skills, higher-order cognitive skills
examples: A pilot MBPA measured the vocational skills of confined space guards, capturing all tasks of the existing PBA using multimedia and interactive tasks
key_sources: Sebastiaan de Klerk, Bernard P. Veldkamp, Theo J. H. M. Eggen. (2018). A framework for designing and developing multimedia-based performance assessment in vocational education. Education Tech Research Dev (2018) 66:147–171. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-017-9559-5

article_title: The Effect of Modeling Based Science Education on Critical Thinking
citation: Bati, K. & Kaptan, F. (2015). The Effect of Modeling Based Science Education on Critical Thinking. Educational Policy Analysis and Strategic Research, 10(1). https://www.inased.org/
title: Modeling Based Science Education Program (MBSEP), a 16-hour electricity unit for 7th grade
description: The MBSEP is an instructional program the authors prepared to explore modeling based science education's influence on critical thinking. It was "designed in the way to include the objectives and the modeling process steps" of the Physical Phenomena Learning Field unit Electricity in Our Lives from the 2005 Turkish 7th grade Science and Technology program, which comprises 32 objectives and 16 class hours. Daily plans and activities covered 16 hours, with special teacher and student forms per activity, and student activity flyers were collected as a qualitative data source.
requirements: Teachers received a 4-hour training on scientific models' roles in science education, the modeling process and the program
Delivery by the regular science and technology teachers within normal class meetings
constraints: The unit was limited to the 7th grade Electricity in Our Lives unit and its 16 class hours
target_learning_goals: Critical thinking skills
Science objectives on electrification and electrical current
examples: Table 1 maps each activity (e.g., How Does Electrification Occur?, What is Electrical Current?) to curriculum objectives and target attainments such as openness to new ideas and creating cause-and-effect relations
key_sources: Bati, K. & Kaptan, F. (2015). The Effect of Modeling Based Science Education on Critical Thinking. Educational Policy Analysis and Strategic Research, 10(1). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1127622

article_title: Mind the Teachers! The Impact of Mindfulness Training on Self-Regulation and Classroom Performance in a Sample of German School Teachers
citation: Rupprecht, S., Paulus, P. & Walach, H. (2017). Mind the teachers! The impact of mindfulness training on self-regulation and classroom performance in a sample of German school teachers. European Journal of Educational Research, 6(4), 565-581. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.6.4.565
title: Logic model: MBSR training improves teacher wellbeing and performance via enhanced self-regulation ability
description: The article proposes a logic model (Figure 1) in which MBSR training increases mindful presence and mindful acceptance, which improve teachers' self-regulation ability, which in turn improves teacher wellbeing and professional performance. The model is grounded in Brown, Ryan, and Creswell's description of mindful awareness as a "foundation for healthy self -regulation." Mediation analyses supported the proposed pathway: changes in mindfulness at post-test fully mediated changes in self-regulation at follow-up for six of eight qualifying outcomes.
requirements: Sufficient home practice to increase trait mindfulness (mediator)
constraints: The model was tested in a small, self-selected, non-randomized pilot sample
Mindfulness did not mediate changes in work engagement
target_learning_goals: self-regulation as professional competence
occupational wellbeing
classroom performance
key_sources: Rupprecht, S., Paulus, P. & Walach, H. (2017). Mind the teachers! The impact of mindfulness training on self-regulation and classroom performance in a sample of German school teachers. European Journal of Educational Research, 6(4), 565-581. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.6.4.565

article_title: Teaching Mindfulness-Based Programs online: perceived costs and benefits.
citation: Burton Alison M., Crane Rebecca S., Griffith Gemma M. (2025). Teaching Mindfulness-Based Programs online: perceived costs and benefits. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-02983-8
title: 50-question online survey of MBP teachers structured around the six MBI:TAC domains
description: A 50-question online survey designed by the research team to capture demographics, teaching experience, practical online teaching matters, and interaction with participants. Pedagogical questions "were based on the six domains of the Mindfulness Based Interventions: Teaching Assessment Criteria (MBI:TAC)". It included 24 qualitative questions, was usability-tested with 18 experienced MBP teachers (eight in a focus group), and took around 20–30 minutes to complete; responses were analysed in SPSS with qualitative content analysis.
requirements: Participants must have delivered at least one MBP fully online and be over 18
constraints: Recruitment via social media and snowballing means the response rate cannot be assessed because the population of active mindfulness teachers is unknown
target_learners: Adult MBP teachers who have taught fully online
target_learning_goals: Understanding teachers' experiences and challenges of online MBP delivery to inform best practice and widen access
examples: The survey opened 8 February 2021 and closed 30 April 2022, gathering data from 109 teachers across 19 countries
key_sources: Burton Alison M., Crane Rebecca S., Griffith Gemma M. (2025). Teaching Mindfulness-Based Programs online: perceived costs and benefits. BMC Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40359-025-02983-8

article_title: Assessing the impact of musical proficiency on percussion note identification skills in undergraduate medical students: an analysis using the Montreal Battery of Evaluation of Amusia.
citation: Chopra Jasneep Singh, Tyagi Ruchi, Reddy Saravanan Sampoornam Pape. (2025). Assessing the impact of musical proficiency on percussion note identification skills in undergraduate medical students: an analysis using the Montreal Battery of Evaluation of Amusia. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06679-w
title: Montreal Battery of Evaluation of Amusia (MBEA) as a measure of musical aptitude
description: The MBEA is "a standardized test that assesses multiple components of music processing", including scale, contour, interval, rhythm, metric, and music memory. In this study it was accessed online through Isabelle Peretz's Lab website and administered to 250 medical students in English, alongside demographic questions on gender, past musical experience, and linguistic preferences.
requirements: Administered via the Peretz Lab online test material; participants judge same/different melodies across six subtasks
constraints: Administered in English in this study, either remotely via Microsoft Forms or on-site with pen-paper mode
target_learning_goals: assessment of musical aptitude and auditory perception components
examples: Used as the musical-aptitude measure correlated against percussion competency and prior training
key_sources: Chopra Jasneep Singh, Tyagi Ruchi, Reddy Saravanan Sampoornam Pape. (2025). Assessing the impact of musical proficiency on percussion note identification skills in undergraduate medical students: an analysis using the Montreal Battery of Evaluation of Amusia. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06679-w

article_title: Advancement in knowledge and skills of nursing students in operation theatre procedures with mobile based learning.
citation: Ahmed Dev Ahrar, Rai Kanika, Sharma Amoldeep, Sarin Jyoti. (2024). Advancement in knowledge and skills of nursing students in operation theatre procedures with mobile based learning. Investigacion y Educacion en Enfermeria. https://doi.org/10.17533/udea.iee.v42n2e15
title: Mobile-based learning application with procedure videos, images, and electronic notes for operating theatre techniques
description: A smartphone application developed as the study's intervention, containing "videos, images, and electronic notes" for four operating theatre techniques: scrubbing, gowning, gloving, and assisting ET intubation. The researcher performed and recorded all procedure videos (durations from 2 minutes 52 seconds to 6 minutes 19 seconds) and uploaded them to the application, whose URL was shared via a WhatsApp group; experimental students had access for two weeks.
requirements: Students must own a compatible smartphone; the study required participants to have their own Smartphone and included only students with android phones.
constraints: The application is exclusively compatible with android phones, which the authors state limited the sample.
target_learners: Undergraduate and post-basic B.Sc. nursing students learning operating theatre procedures
target_learning_goals: Knowledge of operating theatre procedures
Clinical skills in scrubbing, gowning, gloving, and assisting endotracheal intubation
examples: Experimental students installed the application, viewed researcher-recorded videos of the four procedures, and had access for two weeks before post-testing.
key_sources: Ahmed Dev Ahrar, Rai Kanika, Sharma Amoldeep, Sarin Jyoti. (2024). Advancement in knowledge and skills of nursing students in operation theatre procedures with mobile based learning. Investigacion y Educacion en Enfermeria. https://doi.org/10.17533/udea.iee.v42n2e15
